justification: A uses a bold numbered sans heading over serif body text, which gives a stronger heading hierarchy than B's light, thin headings. Otherwise B reads better. It keeps the whole JSON example on one page, while A splits it across A2–A3. B's wider code blocks avoid awkward line wraps such as the hashlib line on A4, and its wider tables keep cells on one line where A3 wraps them. B's header band on B1 also replaces A1's nearly empty cover page.

B's bold sans numbered headings stand out more clearly against the serif body than A's light serif headings. B's slightly larger body text is easier to read, and its running header and footer help orientation. A has a more refined title band and rule-separated sections, but its headings are weaker. Both designs leave the lower half of page 2 empty.

Design A compresses the content into three pages with a compact title band and continuous flow, whereas B spends a full dark cover page and leaves page 2 half empty after the introduction. A's bold sans headings create clearer hierarchy than B's light serif headings. Both share the duplicate References heading and nearly identical tables and charts. A's hanging headings against indented body are slightly odd, but overall A reads more efficiently.

A keeps the problem section intact on page 1, with the chart's follow-up paragraph directly beneath it. Its page 2 has a running header band and a clean section start. B breaks the problem section, stranding its final paragraph at the top of page 2. It also has a weaker running head. Both designs leave page 2 largely empty.

A uses bold numbered sans headings that clearly outrank the body text, and it fits the content compactly on two pages with even fill. B's light serif section headings are barely heavier than its bold subheadings (Phase 1 reads stronger than Approach), which inverts the hierarchy. B also leaves a large empty half-page on B2 after Phase 1 and a mostly blank B4. A's running header showing the current section adds navigation. The tables are comparable in both.

A is the tighter design. It uses a compact header band and runs to 3 pages. The plant image on A2 sits beside the paragraph about paths, hides and a learning shelter, so the image is anchored to text. B adds a full cover page that is mostly empty dark green. B3 then opens with a floating image next to a large blank left column, which leaves awkward dead space. B's serif typography is elegant, but the figure caption on B3 switches to a sans face, which is inconsistent. Both designs have pages that end with large white areas, but B's layout wastes more space.

The two designs share the same structure and content. A sets bold sans headings over serif body text, so the sections stand out more clearly than B's light serif headings (A1, A2 vs B1, B2). A's hanging indent of body text under the headings also gives a crisp left edge. B's single-line title and its chart coloured to match the brand are pleasant touches. Even so, B's thin heading weight weakens scanning, and its colour mixes the wine band with teal rules. Overall A has the slightly stronger hierarchy.

A has an elegant serif cover and a well-scaled note callout, but the note on A2 is oversized and visually louder than the section headings. A5 holds only three changelog lines and leaves most of the page empty. A's code blocks also wrap awkwardly (A3, A4). B is compact across three pages with a header band on B1 and running header and footer bands on B2–B3. Its code lines fit without wrapping and its note callout is properly subdued. B's pages fill evenly; its main weaknesses are the orphaned retry sentence at the top of B3 and the lack of a cover.

A's serif typography is warmer and more refined. Its dedicated cover gives the proposal presence, and the inset quote panel over the marsh image (A2) is well integrated. B's sans text is set light and grey, which reads weaker. The 'Our approach' section breaks awkwardly onto B2 as an orphaned paragraph beside the image. B's dark header and footer bands feel heavy. Both share large empty areas on their final pages, and the tables are equal.

B pairs a bold sans heading with a serif body. This gives clearer section hierarchy and more comfortable reading text, and its quote overlay on the image reads well. A relies on light, thin headings with light grey body text, and its two-tone green pullout split looks slightly heavier. A's running header and footer bands are more polished than B's plain folios. Tables and timeline are comparable in both, and both leave large empty space at the foot of page 3.

A is the more compact and coherent design. On A2 the sea purslane image sits beside its text in a deliberate side-by-side layout, and the Programme follows on the same page. In B3 the same image floats in the right half with an empty left column above Programme, which reads as a layout gap. B's full-page dark cover (B1) is handsome but empty. Its light-weight serif headings are weaker than A's bold sans headings. A's heading-outdented, indented-body structure gives clearer hierarchy. Tables are essentially identical.

A fits the content on three pages and opens with a strong navy title band. Its JSON invoice example stays whole on A2 with its table. B uses a mostly empty cover page (B1) and splits the JSON code block across B2 and B3. B's narrower tables wrap cells such as 'Token missing or expired' (B3), and its webhook code line wraps awkwardly (B4). B's numbered bold headings are a little stronger than A's light headings with rules. Overall, A reads more compactly and cleanly.

A uses a refined serif with light rule-topped headings, giving calm, consistent pacing. B's heavy navy heading bands repeat on every section and crowd the pages. B3 packs four sections tightly, with justified text producing awkward hyphenation ('pro-gramme', 'Me-ridian') and uneven word spacing. Both end on a sparse final page.

B's cover uses the landscape illustration as a strong full-bleed image. Its bold numbered sans headings give clearer hierarchy than A's light serif heads. In B the pull-quote panel sits beside the image rather than covering it. Its header and footer bands frame the pages consistently. A's cover is a mostly empty dark field with small type. Both share the same odd right-floated image on page 3 and similar tables.

B offers a strong full-bleed cover, consistent header/footer bands, numbered headings, and body text aligned to the heading edge. A suffers from awkward hanging-indent body text offset from its headings. A also mixes two body sizes on A1 and uses loosely justified narrow text beside the image on A2. Its quote box covers the landscape image. B's sidebar quote beside the image is cleaner. B's image-alone top of B3 is slightly awkward, but overall B reads more coherently.

B's bold sans headings stand out more clearly against the serif body than A's light serif headings, which nearly blend into the text. B's running section names in the footer also aid navigation. B hangs its headings left of the indented body, which is slightly uneven, and its table cells wrap more, but its hierarchy is stronger. A's dark cover is striking, though both covers work. Overall B scans better.

A uses bold, numbered sans headings that stand clearly above the body text. B's light serif headings are weaker than its oversized 'Note' callout (B2), which inverts the hierarchy. B also leaves large voids, with a half-empty B3 and an orphaned changelog on B5. A packs the content into four even pages. B's dark cover is striking, but overall A reads better.

A fits the content onto three well-filled pages, with numbered headings and a compact flow. B's heavy navy heading bands repeat and break the flow. B2 leaves the lower half of the page empty, and B4 holds only three lines, so pagination is wasteful. B's band styling is bold, but its rhythm and balance suffer.

A opens with a refined full-page dark cover and a serif face, but its lede paragraphs jump to a larger size in both sections (A2, A4), and A2 is left half empty. B fits the title into a compact banner over the abstract and introduction (B1), carries running header bands (B2, B3), and keeps body sizes consistent. Both repeat the 'References' heading. B's tighter rhythm and band system outweigh A's more elegant cover.

A runs body text and headings on a single consistent left edge, uses a chart colour that matches the maroon band, and carries a running header and a 'Page 2 of 2' footer. B hangs its headings out to the left of an indented text column, which leaves the layout looking unanchored. B's black chart clashes with its brand colour, its body text is set in lighter, more widely tracked type, and its table has a heavier rule. B's section dividers do help structure, but overall A reads cleaner and more cohesive.

A uses a restrained serif system with gold rules and a dignified dark cover, and its headings sit aligned with the text column. B's hanging sans headings jut out past the indented body, which looks disjointed. Its loud red band clashes with the scholarly tone, and its body text is widely letterspaced, which hurts readability. Both repeat the 'References' heading. B is more compact, but A reads more cohesively.

Design A hangs its headings at the far left while the body is indented, so the section rules start in the wrong place. Its running footers repeat stale subsection titles, and its text is hyphenated in places (seg-mentation, pro-gramme). Page A4 holds only three lines. Design B uses one consistent left edge and cleaner, unhyphenated serif setting. It keeps the closing sections together on B4 and has steadier footers. A's bold sans headings are punchier, but B is more coherent overall.

B's sans headings over serif text, boxed abstract, running headers and navy chart read more polished and easier to navigate (B2, B3). A keeps table and figure numbering ("Table 1:", "Figure 1:") that B drops for bare small captions. Both duplicate the References heading (A3, B4). B's cover page is mostly empty but conventional. On balance B is the stronger finished document.

A runs in three compact pages with a consistent sans face, a cover band that carries the abstract, and running headers. B spends a whole near-empty dark cover page. It also switches body text size inconsistently, with larger lead paragraphs in its Introduction and Discussion, which breaks the rhythm. Both repeat the duplicated References heading.

A pairs a sans-serif heading face with a serif body, adds running headers and footers, and uses a boxed abstract and a navy chart with a title. This gives clearer hierarchy and a more polished feel. A does use a mostly empty title page. B is a plain LaTeX-style default with dense Times text and a duplicated, equally weighted 'References' heading. B's chart is also stark black. Both duplicate the references heading, but in A the second heading is visually subordinate.

A uses a cohesive serif pairing, a title that fits on one line, and a chart colour that matches the masthead band. B hangs its bold sans headings out into the left margin while the body is indented. This creates an awkward double left edge, and B's black chart clashes with its brighter red band. A's tighter, single-column alignment reads more calmly.

B opens with a full-bleed cover image and title band, then uses bold numbered headings that read clearly against its serif body. A uses light headings with rule lines, which feel weaker. A's page 2 has a short paragraph stranded beside the image, leaving an awkward gap at left. B keeps the approach text together and pairs the image with the programme. However, B's page 3 also leaves the image floating with empty space to its left. B repeats the landscape image on the cover and on page 2. A's sans typography is crisp, but B's overall structure is stronger.

A packs the content compactly into three pages with consistent framing bands and a clean flow of sections. B spends a whole cover page on a title. Its oversized note callout dominates B2, it leaves a large void on B3, and a near-empty Changelog page (B5) wastes space. B's code blocks also wrap awkwardly (B4), and the indented body text breaks alignment with the headings.

A's heavy navy section bands consume space and force awkward breaks. A2 has a large empty bottom half after a single Phase 1 paragraph, and A4 holds only three Next Steps lines on an otherwise blank page. B uses numbered headings and flows the content compactly across B2–B3 with consistent spacing and no stranded fragments. B reads as a tighter, more balanced document.

A opens with a full illustrated cover and keeps each section intact. Its serif body text paired with bold sans headings reads well, and the numbered headings give clear hierarchy. B's light-weight sans headings are weak. B also splits 'Our approach' across pages, leaving a lone paragraph stranded beside the image on B2, which looks unbalanced. A's isolated image at the top of A3 is a minor flaw, but A is more coherent overall.

A keeps one consistent sans text size, with headings aligned to the body column and a calm navy palette carried into the chart and the running header bands. B outdents its headings past the text column and switches to an oversized serif lead paragraph in the Introduction and Discussion, which makes the rhythm uneven. B's bright red cover band clashes with its black chart. Both designs repeat the 'References' heading. A reads more evenly.

B's bold numbered headings (B1, B2) stand out clearly against its serif body text. A's light sans headings sit weakly against the body, and its rule lines add separation without much emphasis (A1, A2). A's solid running band on page 2 is stronger than B's thin rule (A2). However, B's serif body reads comfortably, and its heading hierarchy wins overall. B carries one paragraph onto page 2 while A keeps the chart's follow-up text with it. Both leave a similarly large empty space at the bottom of page 2.

B uses strong numbered sans headings that stand out clearly against the body text. A's thin serif headings with rules carry less weight, and A's oversized Note callout on A2 competes with the section headings. B packs the content into 4 pages and finishes with a full final page. A leaves a nearly empty Changelog page (A5) and a half-empty A3. B's header and footer bands give consistent navigation. Against this, B splits the JSON code block across B2 and B3, a split A avoids. A's dark cover is striking, but overall B reads more coherently.

A pairs bold sans headings with a serif body, so the numbered section heads stand out clearly (A1, A2). B's light serif headings, set under rules, are weaker, and its small, light body text is harder to read (B1, B2). B's one-line title is tidy, but A's running header and 'Page 2 of 2' footer aid navigation. Both have the same large empty space at the bottom of page 2.

B keeps the invoice JSON example in one piece on B3, where A splits it across A2–A3. B also uses lighter running footers and section rules instead of A's heavy dark header and footer bands. Its body text has a more refined indented measure. B has costs: the oversized note on B2 is clunky, and the changelog sits nearly alone on B5. A is more compact, but its broken code block and dense bands hurt reading.

A uses elegant serif headings with rule bands and a clean cover, but its pages break poorly. A2 ends after Phase 1 with half the page empty, and A4 holds two short sections with three-quarters of the page blank. B packs the same content into three pages with numbered sans headings and running headers. Its fill is even, though B2's dense top and some hyphenation feel slightly heavier. A's lighter, sized headings are a touch more refined, but B's pagination and rhythm win overall.

A uses a consistent serif system with headings, body text and tables aligned to one left margin. That gives calm, even pages (A2, A3). B pairs a heavy geometric sans with a serif. Its headings hang outside an indented text column, so the page feels shifted left and unbalanced, with the right margin narrower than the left (B2, B3). B's hyphenation (seg-mentation, pro-gramme) adds ragged breaks. B packs more onto page 3, but it leaves only one short list on B4. A's last page is similarly sparse but cleaner.

A keeps the Creating an Invoice code block whole on A3, and every section in A begins at a clean rule. B breaks that code block across B2 and B3, and the Error Handling note is split from its table across B3 and B4. B's heavy dark header and footer bands on every page crowd the content and push text close to the edges. A's large callout note on A2 is a little oversized, and its changelog leaves A5 nearly empty. B packs its pages more tightly, but the split code and heavy bands outweigh that.

B offers a polished cover, gold rule bands, running footers, a boxed abstract and a larger chart that makes the results easier to take in. Its weaknesses are a large empty half page on B2, lead paragraphs set larger than the body text, and the same duplicated References heading A has. A is plain but consistent, with numbered bold headings. Its pages are unevenly filled (A3 is mostly empty) and its default look is weak. On balance B is the more finished document.

A has a dedicated full-bleed cover with a restrained serif title and accent rule. Its interior pages carry a consistent header band and keep body text aligned with the headings. B crams the title into a header band on page one. Its heads hang outdented while the body is indented, which looks misaligned. B's p2 also has a narrow justified paragraph with loose word spacing beside the image. A's p3 does leave a large empty area left of the image, and A's p4 is bottom-heavy with empty space. Even so, A reads more polished overall.

A pairs a geometric sans for headings with a serif for body text, which reads more comfortably than B's light sans throughout. A's hanging headings with rule lines give a clean, open structure. B's heavy full-width navy section bands repeat on every heading and crowd pages B2–B3, and they compete with its header strip. B's justified light text also shows loose spacing (B3). Both designs share the same weak pagination: page 2 is left half empty and page 4 is nearly empty.

A's heavy navy band headings repeat six times, dominating the pages and crowding the content. Its justified text shows hyphenation such as 'pro-gramme' and 'Me-ridian' (A3). Its running header lags the content: page A2 is labelled 'Phase 1' and page A3 'Phase 2'. B uses quiet rule-topped serif headings that read more elegantly and give an even rhythm. B's tables are clean and its paragraphs run without awkward breaks. B's last page also carries two sections, so it is less empty than A4, which holds three lines.

A's cover uses the landscape illustration to good effect, while B's cover is a nearly empty dark field. A's bold sans headings over serif body give a clearer hierarchy than B's light, unbolded serif headings. B's thin rules and logo are refined, but its body text is small and light. Both share the same awkward right-floating image on page 3.

B keeps headings and body on one consistent left edge, adds a running header and footer, and carries the brand maroon into the chart bars and table rules, which gives the brief a coherent identity. A uses hanging headings with a deep body indent and divider rules, which gives clear section breaks, but its black chart and plain table feel disconnected from the cover band. A's indented text measure is also narrower and less comfortable to read.

A has a polished cover, refined serif typography, gold rules separating sections, and a boxed abstract. Its chart carries a clear title. A has flaws: a sans chart title clashes with the body, there is a duplicated References heading, and A2 leaves a large empty area. B is a plain article layout with good density, but its Times typography is generic. B's Table 1 caption sits cramped against the text, and B also duplicates References, with a big empty space on B3. Overall, A reads as more considered and easier to keep.

A keeps a consistent sans heading and serif body system, with numbered sections and running headers. Its pages fill evenly. B has a striking dark cover, but its section heads are light and weak. B's lead paragraphs are set larger than the paragraphs that follow, so text size is inconsistent. B2 leaves half the page empty, and the repeated gold rules fragment the flow. Both designs duplicate the References heading, but B's small bold version followed by a larger one is more jarring.

A is a compact, consistent academic layout. Its headings are clear, its tables and figure are numbered, and its pages fill evenly. B has an attractive header band and a boxed abstract. However, its abstract labels sit apart from their text, and its light section headings are weaker than its bold header. B also leaves large voids on B1 and B2 and splits Table 2 onto the next page. Both designs duplicate the 'References' heading, but B's light-plus-bold pair (B3) looks more awkward.

A fits the content into two well-filled body pages, with numbered headings and the wave table placed directly under Phase 2. B leaves a large empty gap at the foot of B2, so the table and Phase 2 move to B3. It then spills Next Steps onto a nearly empty B4. B's ruled section dividers and hanging indents look elegant, but the pagination wastes space and breaks the flow.

A pairs bold numbered sans headings with a serif body, so the sections stand out clearly. B uses light, thin headings and a light grey sans body that reads weaker and less crisp. B keeps the chart's follow-on paragraph on page 1, while A carries it over to page 2. That is minor, and both leave similar empty space on page 2.

Both designs share the same content flow and the same large empty areas on pages 2 and 4. A stacks heavy navy full-width heading bands on every section; on A3 there are two of them, and together with the header bar they make the page feel blocky and weighed down. B uses light rules, hanging headings and an indented serif body. That gives a calmer, more editorial page, and the two tables read cleanly in it. B's cover title wraps, which is a minor flaw, and its headings are set slightly off-axis to the left. Even so, its pages balance better overall than A's.

B keeps 'The problem' section together on page 1, so the chart and its follow-up sentence stay with their section. A pushes a single orphaned paragraph onto the top of page 2, which breaks the flow. B also has a running header band and page numbering that orient the reader. A's serif type is elegant, but its title is heavy, and B's sans setting is clean and consistent. A's page 1 leaves slack space below the chart.

B packs the content into three well-filled pages, with numbered headings and running headers. A breaks after Phase 1 and leaves the bottom of A2 half empty. It then strands Next Steps alone on a nearly blank A4. A's deep body indent wastes width and makes the measure uneven.

A opens with a full-bleed cover illustration and keeps each section intact. Its approach paragraphs stay together on A2, and its running header and footer bands are consistent. B squeezes the title into a header band and splits 'Our approach' across pages, leaving an orphaned paragraph beside the image on B2. B's lead paragraph also switches size mid-section on B1, and its outdented headings with hanging indents read less cleanly. A has some empty space at the top of A3 and the bottom of A4, but its overall rhythm is steadier.

A has a strong title band and clear sans headings, but its body text is indented far from the left-hung headings. It also inflates some lead paragraphs into a larger size, which breaks the rhythm. The abstract box crowds its heading into the label. Both designs duplicate the References heading. B is a conventional, consistent academic layout with numbered sections, captioned figure and tables, and an even text measure. Its only flaw is a large empty space at the bottom of pages 2 and 3.

A is consistent and calm. It has a clean title page, numbered headings, uniform body text, and running headers and footers. B packs the page more efficiently, but it is less coherent. Its lead paragraphs switch to a larger size with odd hanging indents (B1, B3). Its headings are outdented far left, and its Mixed logit table is split from its section across pages (B3). It also shows a doubled 'References' heading. The red cover band is striking but jars with the academic tone. A shares the duplicate references heading (A4), but its overall rhythm and hierarchy are steadier.

A has a striking dark cover and elegant serif, but its lead paragraphs switch to a larger size inconsistently, and page A2 is half empty. B uses numbered sans headings with consistent body size and running headers, and packs content evenly across B2–B3. B also starts the chart and table together on B3. Both duplicate the References heading. A's gold rules and cover band are more refined, but B reads more consistently.

A keeps the problem section, including its closing paragraph, together on page 1. Its chart uses the brand maroon, and page 2 carries a running header band and footer. B splits the closing line of the problem section onto page 2 as an orphan. B's black chart clashes with the maroon cover band, and its hanging headings with indented body read slightly less cohesively. B does have stronger heading weight.

A pairs a bold sans heading with a warm serif body, giving clear section hierarchy and comfortable reading. B uses light-weight headings that read weakly, and its justified body text on B1–B3 shows uneven spacing. B's header and footer bands and its side-by-side quote panel are tidy. A's quote overlay on the image and its indented body column still feel more considered. A also has awkward justified text in the picture paragraph on A2, but B's thin type weakens hierarchy throughout.

B is more consistent. It uses one body size with numbered headings and running headers, and its table and chart are styled to match. A uses an oversized lead paragraph in Introduction and Discussion, outdented headings with inconsistent indentation, and a strong red band. A also splits the results table onto A3 away from its chart, and its doubled 'References' heading is more jarring than B's. B's cover page is mostly empty, but its body pages read more cleanly.

A has a dedicated cover page with good weight contrast and clear bold headings. However, its body text is indented away from the headings, and code blocks run past the right margin. Its oversized Note callout dominates A2, and the Changelog is stranded nearly alone on A5. B is denser and more consistent. Its full-width text, tables and code share one measure, the navy title and running header/footer bands are coherent, and the Error Handling table keeps rows on single lines. B's light headings are weaker, and it splits the Error Handling section across pages, but overall it reads more evenly.

A packs the content into three pages, with the title band and the abstract together on page 1, so there is no near-empty cover page. B gives a whole page to a small centred title (B1) and ends with a mostly empty page 4. A's light section headings are weaker than B's bold numbered ones. Both repeat the 'References' heading (A3, B4). Overall, A's flow and use of space read better.

A has bolder sans headings that stand out more clearly, but its headings hang outside an indented body column, so the pages read as misaligned. Its rules overrun the right margin, and body lines are narrow and justified, which gives gappy spacing on A4. B keeps one consistent column with headings aligned to the text and a proper dark cover. A navy top band repeats on every page, and the running footer shows the document title rather than A's mismatched section names. B's light serif headings are weaker, but its overall layout is more coherent.

A packs the content into three well-filled pages. Its code blocks keep their lines intact. The note is a modest callout. Header and footer bands give each page a consistent frame. B gives up a whole page to a mostly empty cover. Its note on B2 is set in oversized type and outweighs the section headings. Code lines wrap awkwardly on B3 and B4, splitting the JSON keys. B3 and B5 leave large empty areas, and the changelog is stranded alone on B5.

A is a plain, consistent academic layout. Its tables and figure carry numbered captions, and its pages are evenly filled. B has an attractive red title band, but it has several problems. The table is split from its caption across pages: the 'Mixed logit estimates' caption floats at the top of B3. The tables lack numbered captions. B1 leaves a large empty bottom, the first paragraphs switch to inconsistent oversized lead text, and the abstract labels are awkwardly stacked. Both designs repeat the 'References' heading, but B's mismatched sizes make the duplication more jarring.

A pairs a serif body with bold sans headings, which gives clear section hierarchy and comfortable reading. Its lead paragraphs are slightly enlarged. B sets section headings in a light-weight sans that barely stands out from the body, and its body text is a dense light sans. B does add running headers and the duplicate 'References' heading reads awkwardly, but A has the same duplication. B's teal rules and navy chart are cohesive, while A's red banner and black bars are less refined. On balance A reads better.

A pairs a serif body with bold sans headings, which gives clear section hierarchy. Its pages flow evenly and the chart sits with its explanatory text (A3). B's thin, light headings are weak, and the 'References' heading is duplicated with mismatched styles (B3). B1 ends with a large empty half-page after the introduction. B's navy cover band is appealing, but A reads more cleanly overall, despite its sparse title page (A1) and a doubled References heading of its own (A4).

Design A leaves the bottom third of page 1 blank because Data and methods is pushed to page 2. Its section headings are light and lack weight. It also has an awkwardly orphaned table at the top of A3. Design B fills its pages evenly: the table sits on B1, and the chart and table flow together on B2. Its headings are numbered and bold, and its figure and table captions are clear. Both designs repeat the References heading. A's dark banner is attractive, but B reads as the more coherent paper.

Design B keeps 'The problem' section whole on page 1, so the paragraph about private loss sits under its chart. A pushes that paragraph alone onto page 2. B also colours the chart in the brand maroon, adds a running header band and a page-numbered footer, and accents the table rules. A's bold serif-paired headings with indented body give it slightly stronger hierarchy. Overall B looks more cohesive and polished.
